default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1298.title: Dollar-led index catch-up
E-1298.hypothesis: WDO and WIN trade inversely; when the dollar makes an unusual move over a window and the index has not yet moved against it, slower index participants catch up in the opposite direction.

E-1299.title: VWAP whipsaw-regime extreme fade
E-1299.hypothesis: Many VWAP crossings in the last hour mean balanced two-way trade; a fresh 20-minute extreme bar in that regime is likely to be rejected, so fade it on the bar's colour.

E-1300.title: Day-open revisit after a big excursion
E-1300.hypothesis: After the price strays far from the day's open and closes back through it, the day's initial balance is lost and the other side gains control; follow the cross.

E-1301.title: Lunch-range breakout
E-1301.hypothesis: The thin midday range is a coiled balance; the first close beyond it after 13:00 follows the arrival of afternoon liquidity and US-session flow.

E-1302.title: Clock-hour open cross
E-1302.hypothesis: Algorithms and desks reference the open of each clock hour; a cross of that level well into the hour signals the direction of the hour's remaining flow.

E-1303.title: VWAP z-score band fade
E-1303.hypothesis: Deviation from VWAP beyond k session standard deviations is stretched against the volume-weighted average price that institutional benchmark orders pull toward; fade it.

E-1304.title: Volatility squeeze break
E-1304.hypothesis: When recent bar ranges are small versus the typical for that time of day, liquidity providers have tightened; the break of the 30-minute range releases stored stops.

E-1305.title: Prior-close reclaim after a dip
E-1305.hypothesis: The previous close is the reference of the overnight positions; after trading away from it by a margin, a close back across it shows the excursion was absorbed; follow the reclaim.

E-1306.title: Wide bar on light volume fade
E-1306.hypothesis: A range much wider than recent bars on below-typical volume is a thin-book air pocket rather than conviction; the move retraces.

E-1307.title: Two-leg momentum acceleration
E-1307.hypothesis: When the latest leg of a move is several times the size of the previous leg in the same direction and larger than typical, forced flows are chasing; follow it.
